Fagan tries to be a nice guy, but not enough for it to actually count. For a class this complex, his curve is very small. He is very particular with his exams, and the content is extremely overbearing. It’s a lot of memorization, even with your two cheat sheets, because of the  questions he asks that arent really resembled in the homework or in class, outside of the general topics.

For me, this was an easy A+ (I got a 99% and I didn't even do a majority of the extra credit). That being said, I am a third year ecology major and this course's content was a repeat of several community college courses I've already taken. Lowest exam grade gets dropped, and the cumulative final is optional and open-note, but I didn't need to take it. Your mileage may vary based on your prior experience with ecology but I'd recommend Dr. Ngeve if you already have a solid understanding like I did. She gives so many extra credit points so just participate in those if your grade is struggling, and study the concepts you aren't familiar with. Some of the homework assignments were laborious but there's only 5 of them. The weekly discussion post is also pretty time-consuming but not difficult.

Like all the other reviews say, Shapiro is pretty good overall. My main gripe is that you have to do really well on exams if you want an A because they make up almost 80% of your grade. The other 20% is based on 7 homeworks (that usually have questions you need to answer on a doc and an associated 5 pt quiz) and a project (tedious but straightforward so you'll likely get full points). He does drop the lowest midterm which is amazing (not including the final). But I've never dreaded multiple choice so much in my life. He makes some of the multiple choice questions confusing (unless you really know the material). They're almost designed to trip you up. The highest I got an a midterm was 92.5 and it was because I got 3 multiple choice questions wrong. Somehow I got all the fill in the blanks, short responses, and diagrams/graphs. To do well on exams, you have to pay attention in class and take good notes. At least he only tests us material covered in class on the powerpoints. Make sure you know everything from vocab, to examples, to graphs/diagrams because they're all fair game. The textbook was very useless for our class because the adaptive quizzes were not mandatory and had no impact on our grade. I did a few of them to help with answering questions based on what I studied, but he doesn't cover everything in the textbook so I could've done without the adaptive quizzes. I wish I didn't waste my money because all we needed were the powerpoints which he posted. He doesn't configurate ELMS to calculate your grade so you need to do that on your own so you're not clueless or blindsided when he puts on final grades. But like I said before, what you get on the exams (not including the one dropped) if pretty much what you'll get in the class. If you get most/all of the points from the homeworks and project your grade will likely increase by a few percents. Overall, the TAs were very helpful and Shapiro is a nice guy. Just watch out for the exams.

BSCI160 is a challenging course, with a massive amount of information to memorize, alongside equations and mechanisms to conceptualize and apply. That said, Dr. Ngeve did an excellent job structuring the course to make success achievable for those willing to put in the effort.

While she moves through the 60+ slides per lecture at a very fast pace and occasionally assigns additional slides for students to review independently, her approach is manageable with consistent effort. She offers ample extra credit opportunities, allowing students with midterm averages around 70% to finish the course with an A. The frequent homework assignments, while not overly time-consuming, are worth a significant portion of the grade and help reinforce key concepts. Additionally, she very generously drops one exam grade, giving many students the option to skip the final. 

Dr. Ngeve is also a genuinely kind and approachable person. She consistently encourages students to reach out with questions and, when approached individually, takes the time to thoroughly explain complex concepts. I also want to shout out the TAs, who were incredibly helpful and accommodating to any extraneous circumstances.

Overall, while the sheer amount of content can feel overwhelming at times, Dr. Ngeve provides the resources and support necessary for all students, including those who struggle with test-taking, to succeed.

pretty goated prof, majority of the bad review on here are because of students who simply couldn't keep up with his lectures. He usually posts the lecture slides a day in advance, and I skimmed them before class which helped me a lot. Although I agree he can be confusing at times, he is usually very responsive to questions during/after class.

Dr.Shapiro is clearly very knowledgeable and passionate about ecology and evolution. Beyond that, I have very minimal positives to say. Like most of the reviews state, he is extremely disorganized in lecture and does not explicitly state what information you're supposed to take away from his extensive tangents. His note slides are very minimal, and often his "examples" are just screenshots of random research articles about the topic he is attempting to lecture on. His homework (only 5 points each) is a complete waste of time. They are often 5-8 questions, however, they take forever to complete because they are very intricate, which is hard to comprehend when you learn nothing but how to sleep with your eyes open during lecture. Additionally, his homework problems do not nearly resemble exam questions (even though he states they do). But I would probably say that the worst part of his class is the exams. They are all structured the same (MC first, followed by fill-in-the-blanks, and then short answer), which is honestly not bad. However, most MC questions are formatted to trick you, and his fill-in-the-blanks are ridiculously specific. He will ask you to recall specific examples or videos he mentioned in lecture for 5 seconds. For example, one of his exam questions asked us to recall what organism a bird was mimicking from a 7-second video we watched in lecture once. His short-answer questions are relatively straightforward, which I can appreciate, and often, you will get partial credit on them for writing practically anything down. Additionally, he offers minimal extra credit (4 points total), which ultimately does nothing to your grade. He does drop your lowest midterm, but when their all extremely low scores, it honestly makes no difference.

Overall, I quite literally would recommend taking any other professor. This class's material is not hard in the slightest, but his class is designed in a way that makes getting an A 10x harder than it should be.

PS: For context, I have taken BSCI170, CHEM131, MATH135, and currently taking CHEM231, MATH136, alongside Dr. Shapiro's BSCI160 lecture, and his class will be the only reason my GPA will drop from a 4.0.

Dr. G is the sweetest professor at UMD. She is extremely helpful if you don't understand homeworks or concepts covered in class, she gives out participation points with clicker questions, and her slides and explanations are really informative. Her exams are way harder than they should be, and you really have to think critically about how topics connect rather than just what the topic is. Overall amazing professor, and if I could have her for other BSCI courses I would. 10/10.

The course was interesting and Dr. Shapiro really cares. Although it is a little boring at times, you really just have to go to class and take notes on everything because there's a chance an example could be on the exam. He let you bring a notecard to examples and a paper for the final which was super helpful as well. His exams were also very fair (although beware of tricky MC questions). Very doable to get a good grade if you just study well for the exams and do the hw. He's also pretty funny and cares about the planet a lot which is really nice to hear about.

I had him last semester and actually teetered on the edge between a A- and an A and ultimately finished with an A because the final was hard and he ended up curving it. I think he is honestly a very much hit or miss professor for many people but I really liked his class. He was really nice and honestly mostly just read off the slides sometimes explaining stuff in more detail. I'm not gonna lie though I genuinely missed the entire 2nd unit and most of the 3rd and still did really well on his exams. I did really bad on the 1st but he ended up curving in the end so it worked out (I think I went from like a 75 to an 83) after that though he only curved the final because he does it based on averages. Like other people said he gives you two pieces of paper front and back and often has review sessions before the exam to go over questions. My only complaint was the math based homeworks were a bit hard for me and dragged my grade down (but for others it really helped like my friend got an A because of the homeworks). 

The way I would study for his exams that really helped me was I would just take 2 days where I would just spend hours going through every single slide and relearning stuff and writing down hard details or important facts (he uses a red color for things you have to memorize so there's no doubt) and doing active recall and actually understanding stuff, so on my sheets I'd have like everything written in tiny font, different colors, terms and definitions, timelines, and trees, basically anything I needed to visually see the content and just understand it. And I found that on the actual exam I never needed it because I learned it so well the first time by condensing and using active recall for the information. I only used the sheets for the specific terms he put on the slides in red where he asked about exact definitions.
I think the way I studied was a bit intense but I did do really well on his exams besides the 1st where I didn't do this study method (I think 2nd exam was a 96 for me and the 3rd was a 95) but also because he did have a 8 point curve built into each exam so around 4 questions which really helped. Though I will say I also studied this way because I skipped so many lectures and would leave the learning till like 2 days before the exam so I think if you start studying ahead of time or just keep up with the content and make the notesheets as studying that would work well too. His exams are basically just based on the slides and in class he might just highlight some things that might be on the exam but he does that on the slides too in writing with little *. 
Overall I think if you learn well from slideshows and are willing to actually learn the material he is a great professor to take and he will really make you learn the stuff. But if you can't do that or don't have the time to really dedicate to learning/memorizing then even his 8 point curve and 2 notesheets won't help.

Dr. G is a very nice human, but her tests ARE SO HARD. She will give you so many options to meet with her but she will not explain herself and will often confuse you. Try to study concepts rather than definition, but that might not even help you. Use Chat to study for tests cause her tests are like the exact same (she prolly uses AI test).

Dr. G is an okay prof, she's nice enough. She has a lot of office hours but doesn't know what she's talking about half the time. She will confuse you. She doesn't have practice exams up and I think most of her exams are written by ai, so use chat to study. Her exams are hard and are very conceptual. There will be fill in the blank question worth 15 points. Good luck.

Not really sure what the negative reviews are talking about. Dr. Garfinkel is a very sweet and very passionate professor. She cares deeply about her students and doing well in the course. It was her first semester teaching, so there were a few hiccups here and there, but overall I think she did a great job. The homeworks are usually a couple pages long, but to be honest they aren't hard as long as you pay attention and take notes. There were no practice exams, probably because she hadn't made exams previously as this was her first semester teaching the course. There were however, study guides for you to review and go over that covered pretty much everything on the exam. The exams are tougher earlier on when talking about genetics and DNA and stuff like that, but they get easier once you're in the big picture stuff. Office hours and the TAs were very helpful, as well as the online textbook. As someone who hasn't sat in a biology class in probably close to five years, I was absolutely worried for my grade in this class. But Dr. Garfinkel was super helpful and there are definitely enough resources that even I was able to pull off getting a B. It's a pretty cool gen Ed, especially since it relates to a lot of modern day issues. Would def recommend if you need a science credit.

Dr. G has got to be one of the best professors in the bio department! She holds lots of office hours throughout the week and every time I've attended, she was super helpful! She genuinely cares about how well students do in her class and wants to help out as much as she can! There are 7 hw assignments throughout the semester which are pretty spread out and can be a bit hard, but there are also clicker questions every class and exam reflections after each one which are a pretty helpful grade booster. She also provided study guides for each exam that accurately reflect what material will be on the exam. Overall, Dr. G is a great professor and I would definitely take a class with her again!

Dr. G is a great professor! Her lectures are super informative, and her slides are well-organized and easy to follow. You don’t really need to buy the online textbook to do well in the class. She and the TAs offer several office hours each week, and they’re extremely helpful— they are really beneficial if you are confused on the HW, want clarification on a topic, or are studying for the exam. She also provides study guides, allows a notecard or sheet of paper during exams, and drops your lowest midterm grade. Definitely use these resources to be successful in the class and on exams, as they are worth 25% of your grade. Overall, she’s really nice, clearly cares about her students, and is very approachable and easy to talk to. I’d definitely recommend taking her class!

dr shapiro is very knowledgable and seems very confident on his expertise in ecology and evolution. however, i sometimes think he is TOO smart for the rest of us taking his class. his exams are by far the worst as he typically includes something that he briefly mentioned in lecture or asked us to recall something so specific from a video (which i think is ridiculous). if you dont go to class, youll likely miss something he said that will definitely be in the exam. he goes on too many tangents and can never just get to the point. he also talks about those stupid birds way too often. aside from the fact that he is a really bad lecturer, he also doesnt let us see our full grade for the whole semester so youre basically blindsided until he releases them. i strongly recommend taking any other professor than him if you actually want to get an A in a 100 level biology class.

Vadim was a pretty good professor. His lectures were easy to follow, exams were fair, and course load was never overbearing, which is all I can ask from a Gen-ed. Attendance was *technically* not mandatory, but about 60-70% of lectures had in-class assignments to be done in small groups. They were always easy, and I'm pretty sure everyone that attended class always got a perfect score, but I didn't love that aspect. He also would not say if there would or would not be an assignment beforehand, though I assume that is because he knew many people would not attend if they knew there were no assignment.

Exams had review sessions with the TA, and the recording and slideshow were posted on ELMS, which made studying pretty quick and straightforward. You were also allowed 2 sheets of notes, front and back, for each midterm, as well as 4 for the final. Lowest exam was dropped, which was really nice. Much of the class didn't even need to take the final. 

Lastly, this was one of Vadim's first semesters teaching, and he really pushed for honest feedback from us, which I think highlights his passion as well as him wanting to improve his class for future years. If I were to take this class again, I'd choose Vadim's class again.

I'm not sure why Dr G is getting any hate at all. Dr G is a truly accommodating and understanding professor. She teaches BSCI160 thoroughly, and her passion shines through her teaching, which can sometimes lead to a muddier barrier between required information and course material. Instructions can be a little unclear on assignments or tests, but she is always there to clear things up, whether it be through email or office hours. This was her first semester teaching at UMD, so I'm sure the clarity of the material will improve for the upcoming semester. I recommend taking her, plus she's fun to talk to.

Shapiro is not a good teacher at all. He is obviously very passionate about the subject but he makes it impossible to get a good grade. I'm someone who is great at bio and aced micro and cell and molecular, yet the way Shapiro sets his class up makes you feel so dumb. He goes on tangents about nothing and expects you to remember these for the tests because he always references something niche that he talked about once, he turns the lights off so you'll fall asleep, and he talks very fast. He seems like a nice person but his powerpoints are literally pictures with no words so it is impossible for you to understand what he wants and his tests are way too hard. Do not take him.

He's an ok lecturer. I thought I understood the concepts raised in class, but no matter how much I studied and jotted down every single thing he mentioned, and went to every single class, I could not get higher than an 80 on his exams. His slides were basically all pictures, and he didn't record lectures, so you had to go to class to understand. His tests are purposely designed to trick you and, most of the time, make no sense, no matter how much you know the topic. The worksheets weren't bad, but as someone who got an A in BSCI170 and even harder science classes like anatomy, I could not do good on his exams for the life of me.
Her exams were unnecessarily hard.
Horrible exams. Does not curve either.

I want to start by saying that Dr. Rankin really is very nice. It's clear that all of the decisions she makes regarding the class are in an attempt to help students succeed, and she is VERY knowledgeable/passionate about the subject she is teaching. That being said, everything about this class stressed me out from beginning to end. The homework for this class was interesting, and I learned a lot from it, but it rarely helped at all with what you would see in the exams later on. She would also give practice quizzes, which were helpful in the sense that you would see what her exam style would be like, but they still didn't really help all that much. The only way I can describe the actual exams is hell on Earth. If Lucifer himself were to wake up one day and say, "Hey ^w^ I'm going to make an exam for these damned souls," they would look like the ones we took in this class. In fact, the whole class did so poorly on the first exam that she actually decided that she would let us retake it two days later, without changing the questions at all, because the average was like 40-50%. I learned after the first time that the only way to do well on the exams in this class is to take notes on every last slide in the presentations (50-80 slides each + many of the slides are just walls of text in size 12 font) and memorize, memorize, memorize as much as you can and then pray. I took BSCI170 last semester without having taken a biology or chemistry class since my freshman/sophomore year of high school, and I barely struggled at all in that class compared to what I have dealt with in this class thus far. I feel bad saying all of this because again, Dr. Rankin is so nice and so incredibly intelligent, but I have yet to meet anyone in my class of 100+ people that have said her teaching style works for them. It feels like 30 years have been taken off my life.

Listen Professor Garfinkel is a really nice woman. She is great at lecturing and is really kind to all her students. That being said her exams are very hard and lengthy. I know several people who submitted multiple pages blank on the first exam. There is lots of writing portions and each exam covers a ton of chapters.

The exams are way too difficult for a 100-level course. This class is structured in a way that makes getting an A 10 times harder than it should be, especially with no curve. This class shouldn’t be the Hunger Games.

Dr. Rankin is super sweet and clearly very knowledgeable, but she teaches the class like we’re PhD students. The amount of depth she goes into is honestly ridiculous for an intro-level course - the class is insanely hard. For some people, this is their very first bio class - as a Biology lover, I feel bad for them because this is their first impression of biology, as it feels like we’re being thrown into a graduate-level course.

Our first midterm? 40 questions in 45 minutes. Some of them required calculations — no calculator allowed. Every question was multiple choice, but not the normal kind where you can guess or eliminate answers. Nope. Each question had like 5–8 options, sometimes including “2 of the above,” “3 of the above,” and “all of the above”… all in the same question. The class average was somewhere between 30–40%. And guess what — she refuses to curve because she “doesn’t believe in curving.”

She’s clearly from a different era of education, and while her experience is impressive, she really needs to understand that those old-school methods just don’t work for today’s students or the way we learn now.

After our first exam, she said she was “disappointed” with the test scores and offered to let us retake the exact same test. When people raised their hands to explain why we struggled — like how we didn’t have enough practice problems or how some questions clearly needed calculators — she literally cut everyone off and said, “I’m not asking for your critiques right now, I just need a yes or no for the retake.”

Her lectures are brutal. Three times a week, she stands in front of a screen and reads straight from her PowerPoint. Each lecture has its own deck — anywhere from 50 to 100 slides — and every slide is just a wall of text in size 12 font. She also uploads extra videos of herself talking outside of lecture, plus textbook PowerPoints that are another 25+ pages each.

On top of that, she made us pay for two external tools outside our school:

SimBio – about $90, with 3 assignments per week that each take 1.5–2 hours. They’re fine, but completely useless for the exams because the questions are way easier.

PointSolutions – aroundt $30 AND NOT MENTIONS IN REQUIRED COURSE MATERIALS, where she asks 1 or 2 random questions during lecture (sometimes none at all), and we have to respond through the app. It’s graded, so if you miss a class, and/or get the question(s) wrong, you lose points.

After the first midterm, even the students who used to sit up front realized there was no point in paying attention. Now everyone just sits in the back and takes their own notes because listening to her read slides does nothing.

Again, Dr. Rankin is a very nice person, and very knowledgeable, but the way this class is structured is just not it...

I absolutely love this professor; she is super sweet, and her exam study guides are very helpful in reviewing for the tests! This course is a lot of work, but she made me excited every day for biology! Would definitely recommend going to her office hours as well because she really breaks down the key concepts in ways that are much easier to understand, and her office hours leading up to the exams you have to go to! She is deliberate in what she talks about during those review sessions to help prepare everyone for the test!
His lectures were easy to follow and the exams were fair. One exam was dropped and another was curved, so many students didn’t even need to take the final.

Professor Garfinkel herself is really nice, and she is super sweet. The content though, is another story. There are 70 slides each class, with about 10 review questions for each lecture as well. The exams are not curved, and really hard. Although, I will say if you go to her office hours it helps SO MUCH. If you take her it won't be the end of the world, you will just have to make sure to review the lectures after every class if you want an A.

All the past reviews? They stay in the past. Participation points? Dropping your lowest midterm grade? Not anymore. So don’t go in trusting old reviews (Spring 2025 was her first semester teaching, which is why she was SUPER lenient with grading back then).

That being said, her exams are very conceptual, so make sure you truly understand the material rather than just memorizing it. Her recommended study methods include making concept maps and using ChatGPT to generate practice exams, since it can create questions similar to the ones she may ask.

She does a really good job making new information more digestible, so I’d recommend going to her office hours if you feel like you’re falling behind. While it’s not impossible to get an A, it is quite difficult and requires extensive studying outside of class.

Lastly, if I were to take this class again, I’d choose Garfinkel’s class again. The third exam was much more direct compared to the first two and was truly reflective of the difficulty expected in a 100-level course. She also mentioned in her office hours that she wouldn’t be including some of the math questions on the final exam. This shows how receptive she was to the feedback she received about improving the course.

The instructor is terrible. In every single aspect of teaching, I would give her a 0/10. I had a horrible teacher last year (senior year of high school) for calculus, and I would complain about her all the time at home, and I remember thinking she was the worst teacher possible. I could not be more wrong. Dr. Rankin is the worst of the worst. 

But before I trash her in this essay, I want to say a few good things. 
1. She is very nice and genuinely cares about your learning.
2. She tries very hard to be accommodating to everyone
3. She is very knowledgeable
4. She provides a study guide

The tests are extremely difficult, even though they're all multiple choice (except one, which had short answers), with each answer many times having all of the above or two of the above or none of the above as answer choices, making each question extremely time-consuming and unnecessarily challenging. Now, with such confusing answer choices, surely the questions were easy, right? Nope. But I get it right, it's a college-level class, you should be prepared for difficulty. But the sheer amount of material you must not just understand, but master, in this class is inconceivable. I'm gonna try to explain it, but I don't think I can truly put it into words. Let's take the second exam, for example. This one unit (unit 2) had more material than YOUR (yes, your) high school bio class by about 3 fold. The study guide she made was 13 pages long, and she didn't finish it because it was "taking her too long". I'm not joking, she literally couldn't finish the study guide, which is just a list, a list, a fricking list of things we need to not just know, but master. I kid you not, one of the bullet points on this 13-page list was "Know the general changes that happened over the history of the Earth", and that's just an example, we also had to know basically every single organism that has ever existed and the phylogenetic tree they are a part of. And there's much more (which I won't get into, because it would take 13 pages of writing). And that's just unit 2 (there are 3 units)

Now, let's talk about lectures. I went to every single lecture and every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday at 1:00 PM. When my lecture ended, I was furious. Her slides are extremely wordy, and she talks very slowly, and her sentences are often broken with frequent stutters and pauses. You might be thinking, Oh, that sucks. She must be so slow. Wrong. She goes through these slides at light speed, often going through 50-80 slides per lecture (in 50 minutes). I don't know how it's possible to talk so slowly and go through slides so quickly. I honestly can't explain it; you just have to see it for yourself. There's also a fun little aspect of her lectures called PointSolutions, which is essentially an app we were required to purchase (cost $60 for a subscription, I believe) where she can quiz us randomly during lectures. You have 30 seconds to answer, and the questions are graded. It's like Kahoot but from hell. It is often super buggy, and she forgets to give us the access code, like once every two lectures, so most people ended up with like a really bad grade on point solutions (which is supposed to be a grade booster). 

Now, let's talk about homework. This class uses a website called SimBio, where sections of a textbook or interactive experiments/games are assigned for homework. It's pretty organized and makes sense, except they are extremely time-consuming. Most classes get these assignments very infrequently and are given a lot of time to complete them, but not Rankin's class. We had one assigned after every single lecture. Oftentimes, it was more than one, even getting up to three sometimes.  

I spent about 70% of this semester working on nothing but this class, and it was still my worst grade by far

Wow, that is a lot of horrible stuff. But I didn't even get to the worst part yet

THERE IS NO CURVE. 

Please, for your sake, do not take this professor. Not even the most pain-crazed masochist would. 
But if you get stuck with her, here is some advice: Don't take notes in class; instead, just listen to what she is saying and go back over the lecture slides and take notes then. Lecture notes are much more important than SimBio assignments. Do the SimBio's if you can, but prioritize the class notes. Use the study guide she provides. Good luck, and may God have mercy on your soul, because she won't.

Have had a good experience in this class overall. Easy assignments (study plan and reflections) and simbio quizzes (online), and exams are pulled straight from lectures. She explains well but moves fast sometimes, but all lectures are recorded and posted (really helpful when you want to go over content before exam) so you can always watch again. 3 midterms (one is dropped) and one final, the midterms are very straightforward.

Garfinkel is a really good professor; she provides a lot of resources to make sure you understand the content well, including study guides, random links, and her office hours are so informative- she will definitely break things down and make sure you understand. She's very nice. My personal experience with her first exam was not great; it was lengthy, and I didn't answer everything, but you could honestly say that's because I didn't use enough of the resources she offered. If you intentionally study her exams become way easier to manage, so don't let the workload intimidate you because beyond that, the class is fine. It will surely humble you, though.
She was a TA for Garfinkel's BSCI160 class, and she does everything she can to support the success of her students. Her review session greatly contributed to my performance on the third exam.

We have 3 midterms, she drops the lowest one. We have 4 30pt interactive tutorial assignments and she drops the lowest one too. She posts slides and records lectures, all she does during lectures is go over and explain the slides. The classes before an exam she does study sessions on each topic with the TAs. The TAs do a good job of going over the material but the teacher herself only goes over questions anybody has instead of reviewing/reteaching that topic. Overall boring class but she posts the slides and lecture recordings on canvas so you don't have to go to every class until exam day.

Very sweet, cares about her students, but she doesn’t curve nor drop any exam grades. She also posts recorded lectures which are great to review before exams. I think her exams are fair and definitely go over what she talks about during lecture.

I honestly don't even know what grade I will be getting in this class right now, since your overall grade in Canvas is either hidden or incorrect. However, I really don't expect to get an A because this class has truly been so horrible. I do want to say, as many others have written, that Professor Rankin is extremely intelligent and kind; however, I would absolutely not recommend taking this class with her. I have not missed a single class all semester and take notes on things that she makes seem important, but nothing will help you on the tests. I don't even know why I put time into this class anymore because most people fail/get extremely low scores on every exam. The tests are all multiple choice, but they aren't questions like you're probably used to; there are typically four actual answer choices, with three other options reading "two of the above", "all of the above", or "none of the above" (or some variation of this). Even if you genuinely know the material (which I would say most feel they do because the concepts of this class are very basic), you probably will never end up with the score you want. She made us retake the first exam because the scores were so bad, and on the second exam (which was so, so content-heavy, it was crazy), she allowed for an index card with notes written down, and most people did even worse on this exam than the first. She has asked for our feedback about what goes wrong on the exams, and when we give feedback about how the format is extremely difficult to interpret, she says she "isn't asking for criticism about her exams." All the reviews for past years say the exact same thing, so I am so surprised nothing has changed, and I assume nothing ever will. She also made us buy a $30 subscription to a live polling website that doesn't even work most of the time, and she has now decided it won't count toward our overall grade (which would have hurt most people's grades anyway, but the fact that we had to pay that much money for no reason is very annoying). Most of the people taking this class are biology majors and pre-med, which makes this all even more concerning because most cannot take a low grade in this 100-level class. She goes so fast over important material, so it's really hard to take good notes, and also her PowerPoint presentations are so long and content-heavy that she doesn't finish them most of the time and records them for us to watch after class. Dr. G is a great professor. Her lectures are pretty entertaining, her exams are not super difficult, and she provides resources. The only thing I would say as a negative is that at the beginning of an exam (usually half multiple choice worth 5pts each, half free response) she would say to not write a lot in the free response section; however, she would take off points if you were not specific enough. 
Otherwise, she is super sweet, and you can tell she really wants her students to succeed. I would recommend her as a teacher.

Pros:

- Homework (15%) and the final project (10%) are straightforward and easy to score well on.
- You get an index card for midterms and a full sheet for the final (don't rely on these like i did, make sure you acc study and understand everything)
- He drops 1 midterm that you scored the lowest on (i failed one so this one got dropped)

- He only gives two extra credits in the beginning of the sem that can only bump you 1%
- i needed a 96 on the final to get an A which is crazy but somehow after putting in a lot of work, i got it! throughout the sem i believed i was gonna get a B+ because i was doing alright, however, I started studying earlier and a lot more which helped.
- Make sure you understand every single example in class

For the first few biology course I took at UMD, Dr. G made BSCI 160 a very fun and a class I look back upon. The content may seem like a lot of memorization, but she allows a notecard as the "cheat sheet" for the exams. I would highly recommend her class because her office hours were accessible and she even had one right after lecture which I thought was very helpful since the information was fresh in our minds. She records her lectures, which I think is very helpful when reviewing slides and can't fully understand/remember a topic or question. She is very kind and will talk one on one with whatever you may be confused about.

Her exams are pretty fair in my opinion and I would definitely recommend her because her teaching is very good because I saw a huge improvement from getting an okay score about an 80% (B-) on the first exam, to getting an improved 99% (A+) on the final exam. 2. Make the notecard in an easy and organized way to understand (use some color)

4. She does have review sessions and ask her questions!

He's okay, does a fine job with teaching, just very much not my style. Very matter of fact and tends to use examples to explain concepts more than actually explaining the concepts. Assignments aren't hard and neither are exams (you get two pages of cheat sheets, front and back). You get in class worksheets which are kind of annoying but he provides the answers so it doesn't really matter.

Dr. G is one of the best Biology professors at UMD... Not only is this a very fun class, but Dr. G is such a sweet professor. She ACTUALLY helps students learn. I started with a low low B on my first exam, with getting almost a 100 on the final. The improvement in her class was amazing.

Tips for success!
1. Make your 3x5 index card cheatsheet in advance (DON'T Cram! Most first year students fall into this trap!)
2. Use the provided study guides (Hint: they help as they are a structure for exams!)

5. There are multiple TAs, and for my year, they had two sections, so double the TAs (we had access to the other section's TAs)
6. Dr. G hosts some review session office hours! (Also her office hours in general were pretty accessible!)

I was amazed at how Dr. G actually helps you learn... 10/10 would highly recommend for BSCI160
